# Marking Guide — LRN International GCSE Artificial Intelligence (7923)

**For examiners and internal assessors. Applies to Paper 1 (written) and Paper 2 (combined internal assessment).**

---

## 1. Assessment Objectives

| AO | What it rewards | Paper 1 | Paper 2 | Overall |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **AO1 — Knowledge and Understanding** | Recall and secure understanding of AI concepts, terminology, tools and historical context. Correct use of technical vocabulary (e.g. *feature*, *label*, *training data*, *inference*, *actuator*, *knowledge base*). | 50% | 0% | 25% |
| **AO2 — Application** | Applying AI methods and tools to solve real-world problems in familiar contexts. Choosing a suitable technique/platform *for a stated purpose*. | 0% | 50% | 25% |
| **AO3 — Analysis and Evaluation** | Analysing the design, effectiveness and ethical implications of AI systems; weighing advantages against limitations; reaching justified conclusions. | 50% | 0% | 25% |
| **AO4 — Practical and Project Skills** | Designing, implementing, testing and presenting AI solutions using accessible tools; documentation, collaboration, reflection. | 0% | 50% | 25% |

**Consequences for marking:**

- Paper 1 is split 50/50 between AO1 and AO3. Section A (50 marks) is predominantly AO1 with AO3 in the 20-mark extended response; Section B (50 marks) is predominantly AO3. **In Section B, factual recall alone cannot reach the top bands** — a candidate who accurately describes what a knowledge-based system *is* but never compares, weighs or concludes has met AO1 in an AO3 question and must be capped.
- Conversely, in Section A short-answer items, do not withhold marks because a candidate has not evaluated. If the command word is "define", "describe" or "identify", accurate content earns the mark.
- Paper 2 carries no credit for knowledge recited in isolation. A report that explains what machine learning is, without evidence of the candidate's own build, testing and reflection, scores in the Low band across Components A and B.

---

## 2. Paper Structure

### Paper 1 — Written Examination (50% of qualification)
**Duration: 1 hour 45 minutes. Total: 100 marks.**

**Section A — Knowledge and Understanding (50 marks)**

| Q | Type | Marks |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Multiple choice, 5 items, tick one answer | 5 (1 each) |
| 2 | Short answer, 5 items, "answer in complete sentences" | 10 (2 each) |
| 3 | Structured response, 3 parts | 15 (5 each) |
| 4 | Extended response — **candidate chooses ONE of two options**, each with three bulleted sub-requirements | 20 |

**Section B — Analysis and Evaluation (50 marks)**

| Q | Type | Marks |
|---|---|---|
| 5 | Case study analysis, four parts (typically 4 + 4 + 6 + 6) | 20 |
| 6 | Comparative evaluation of two AI techniques, three bulleted sub-requirements | 10 |
| 7 | Logical reasoning: (a) truth-table completion, (b) applied explanation | 10 (4 + 6) |
| 8 | Extended evaluation of a statement — balanced argument with stated conclusion | 10 |

Timing guidance for judging expectations: roughly one mark per minute, leaving reading time. A 20-mark extended response is expected to run to 20–25 minutes of writing — do not penalise brevity per se, but a response of two or three sentences cannot demonstrate the coverage the band descriptors require.

### Paper 2 — Combined Internal Assessment (50% of qualification)
**Internally assessed under supervised and guided conditions, externally moderated by LRN. Total: 100 marks. Approx. 20–25 hours.**

- **Component A — AI System Build (40 marks):** Problem definition (5†), tool/platform selection (5†), data preparation (10), model training and testing (10), performance evaluation and improvements (10).
- **Component B — Project Documentation (30 marks):** Explanation of system and objective (5), step-by-step process (10), evaluation of results (5), visuals/screenshots/code (5), ethics and user awareness (5).
- **Component C — Presentation & Collaboration (30 marks):** System presentation (10), format (5), collaboration (5), shared tools (5), personal reflection (5).

† **Note a live discrepancy:** the Paper 2 task sheet allocates 5 marks each to problem definition and tool selection, while the Assessment Form instructs "Mark each criterion out of 10" for all five Component A criteria (5 × 10 = 50, not 40). Markers must follow the **task-sheet weightings** (5/5/10/10/10 = 40) and use the rubric's High/Medium/Low descriptors proportionately for the 5-mark criteria. Flag any centre that has used the 10-mark scale for problem definition or tool selection.

**Grade thresholds (adaptable by cohort):** 90–100 = 9; 80–89 = 8; 70–79 = 7; 60–69 = 6; 50–59 = 5; 40–49 = 4; 30–39 = 3; 20–29 = 2; 10–19 = 1; 0–9 = U.

---

## 3. Level / Band Descriptors

### 3.1 Paper 2 — the published rubric wording (use verbatim)

Paper 2 is the only component for which LRN publishes explicit level descriptors. They are structured as **High (Excellent) / Medium (Satisfactory) / Low (Basic) / No Credit**.

**Component A (10-mark criteria: High 9–10, Medium 6–8, Low 1–5, No Credit 0)**

| Criterion | High (9–10) | Medium (6–8) | Low (1–5) | 0 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Problem definition | "The problem is identified, specific, and realistic" | "The problem is defined but lacks clarity or scope" | "The problem is vague or too broad" | "No clear problem defined" |
| Tool/platform selection | "The tool is appropriate, well-justified, and used effectively" | "The tool is somewhat appropriate; justification is limited" | "The tool is inappropriate or poorly used" | "The tool was not selected or not used" |
| Data preparation | "Data is well-cleaned, correctly labelled, structured, and fit for purpose" | "Some cleaning/structuring done, some issues remain" | "Data is poorly prepared or disorganised" | "No preparation or incorrect use" |
| Model training and testing | "The model is trained with relevant data and tested correctly" | "Training/testing attempted, but lacks completeness or quality" | "Basic training or testing attempted, with limited success" | "No evidence of training or testing" |
| Evaluation and improvement | "Model's performance is well-evaluated, with clear refinements made" | "Some evaluation and minor improvements made" | "Weak evaluation; unclear or no improvement attempts" | "No evaluation or improvements made" |

**The decisive discriminators in Component A:** the word *justified* (tool selection), *fit for purpose* (data), *tested correctly* — i.e. on data held separate from training data, per spec 6.1.4 — and *refinements made* (not merely proposed). A candidate who evaluates thoughtfully but changes nothing is Medium, not High.

**Component B (High 5, Medium 3–4, Low 1–2, No Credit 0)**

| Criterion | High (5) | Medium (3–4) | Low (1–2) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Explanation of AI system | "Clear purpose, context, and functionality are described" | "General explanation given, lacks some detail" | "Vague or unclear purpose or explanation" |
| Step-by-step process (×2, /10) | "The process is clearly explained, logical, and thorough" | "Mostly clear process, with minor gaps" | "The process lacks clarity or contains major gaps" |
| Evaluation of results | "Critical and accurate interpretation of model results" | "Some attempt at interpretation, lacks depth" | "Basic or incorrect interpretation" |
| Visuals/screenshots/code | "Clear, relevant, and enhances understanding" | "Included, but not always clear or helpful" | "Minimal or poorly explained visuals/code" |
| Ethics and user consideration | "Thoughtful reflection on ethics, bias, privacy, and user impact" | "Basic mention of one or two issues" | "Vague or irrelevant discussion" |

Note the ethics discriminator: **naming** bias and privacy is explicitly Medium ("basic mention of one or two issues"). High requires *reflection* — i.e. relating the issue to this system, its users and its data.

**Component C (High 5, Medium 3–4, Low 1–2, No Credit 0)**

| Criterion | High (5) | Medium (3–4) | Low (1–2) |
|---|---|---|---|
| System presentation (×2, /10) | "Clear explanation, well organised, confident demonstration" | "Mostly clear with some hesitancy or missing details" | "Unclear or rushed explanation" |
| Format | "Professional, engaging, appropriate medium used" | "Appropriate format used but basic" | "Poor formatting or presentation method" |
| Collaboration (if applicable) | "Shared roles clearly defined and well-coordinated" | "Some evidence of collaboration" | "Minimal contribution; poor teamwork" |
| Use of shared tools | "Effective use of collaboration tools (e.g. Docs, Git, folders)" | "Some evidence of shared tools" | "Limited or inappropriate tool use" |
| Personal reflection | "Honest, thoughtful review of own work and learning" | "Some reflection, limited depth" | "Minimal or unclear reflection" |

Where a candidate works solo, "Collaboration (if applicable)" cannot be zeroed by default — award on the basis of teacher observation log evidence of shared working, peer feedback or role definition; if genuinely no collaborative element was possible, the centre must document this and the criterion is assessed on use of shared tools and organisational evidence.

### 3.2 Paper 1 — banding the extended items

The Paper 1 mark scheme gives **indicative content only** ("Mark Scheme: 20 marks") with no published levels. Apply the following levels-of-response framework consistently, keyed to the bullets printed under each question, since each extended question specifies its own required strands.

**Q4 — 20-mark extended response (three bulleted strands)**

| Band | Marks | Descriptor |
|---|---|---|
| 4 | 16–20 | All three bulleted strands covered in depth and in correct sequence/relationship. Accurate, confidently used technical terminology throughout. Sustained exemplification (named tools, named metrics, a concrete worked scenario). Some analysis of *why* stages matter — e.g. why test data is held out, why a deployed model is monitored. Coherent, well-structured prose. |
| 3 | 11–15 | All three strands addressed, at least two in reasonable detail; the third may be thin. Terminology largely accurate. At least one developed example. Clear structure; minor omissions or imprecision. |
| 2 | 6–10 | Two strands addressed, or all three treated superficially. Description without explanation. Generic or absent examples. Some terminology confusion (e.g. training/test data conflated). |
| 1 | 1–5 | One strand only, or a list of unconnected points. Everyday language rather than subject terminology. |
| 0 | 0 | Nothing creditworthy. |

**Q6 — 10-mark comparative evaluation (three bulleted strands)** and **Q8 — 10-mark extended evaluation**

| Band | Marks | Descriptor |
|---|---|---|
| 4 | 9–10 | All bulleted strands covered. For Q6: explicit **comparison** — statements set the two approaches against each other on storage/use of knowledge, flexibility/adaptability, and applications, with valid examples of each. For Q8: genuinely **balanced** — advantages and risks both developed, plus a **conclusion that is justified by the preceding argument**, not merely asserted. |
| 3 | 6–8 | Most strands covered; comparison or balance present but one side is thinner. Examples given but may be generic. A conclusion is reached but with limited justification. |
| 2 | 3–5 | Both approaches/sides mentioned but treated separately with little or no comparison; or one side only, developed. Little or no conclusion (Q8). |
| 1 | 1–2 | Isolated valid point(s); largely descriptive; no evaluation. |
| 0 | 0 | Nothing creditworthy. |

**Q8 specifically: a response with no conclusion cannot exceed Band 3 (max 8), and a one-sided response cannot exceed Band 2 (max 5)** — the question explicitly demands "a balanced argument" with "your conclusion and justification". A conclusion of the form "AI should assist but not fully replace human oversight" is fully creditable *if the preceding paragraphs support it*.

**Q5(c) and Q5(d) — 6-mark case-study items.** These are best treated as *point-plus-development*: typically 2 marks for each of two examples/suggestions (1 for identification, 1 for development in the drone/urban context) plus 2 marks for evaluative or contextual comment. Where the stem says "include at least two examples", a single well-developed example is capped at 4.

---

## 4. Command Words

| Command word | What must be present | Typical mark pattern |
|---|---|---|
| **Identify / State / Name** | The correct item only. No explanation required; do not withhold marks for lack of elaboration. | 1 mark each |
| **Define** | A technically accurate statement of meaning using appropriate terminology. Where the stem adds "and give one example", the example carries its own mark. | 1 + 1 |
| **Describe** | An accurate account of features, stages or characteristics — *what* happens. No causal reasoning required. | 1 per accurate point, or point + development |
| **Explain** | Reasons or mechanism — *why* or *how*. A description alone caps at half the available marks. E.g. "explain the purpose of a sensor" requires the link from detection → decision → autonomous action, not just "it detects things". | Point + linked reason |
| **Compare** | Explicit relational statements addressing *both* subjects on the *same* criterion. Two separate descriptions do not constitute a comparison and cap at Band 2. | Levels |
| **Evaluate / Discuss** | Consideration of more than one position, with weighing, and a judgement. Both strengths and limitations expected. | Levels |
| **Analyse** | Breaking a system or scenario into components and showing how they interact or affect outcomes. | Levels |
| **Justify** | A claim supported by reasoning and, where possible, evidence or an example. Unsupported assertion earns nothing. | Point + support |
| **Suggest** | A plausible, context-appropriate proposal. Credit valid responses outside the mark scheme provided they fit the scenario. | Point + development |
| **Complete** (truth table, flowchart) | All cells/steps correct. Marks are per row/step. | 1 per row |
| **Write a balanced argument** | Both sides *plus* a stated, justified conclusion. See Q8 cap above. | Levels |
| **Include:** (bulleted stems) | Each bullet is a required strand. Omitting a bullet entirely places the response in a lower band. | Levels |

---

## 5. Marking Conventions

1. **Positive marking.** Award marks for what is creditworthy. Never deduct marks for incorrect additional material *unless* it directly contradicts a creditworthy statement — where a candidate gives two contradictory answers to a single-point item, neither is credited.
2. **Alternatives to the model answer.** The published mark scheme answers are **indicative, not exhaustive**. Any technically correct, contextually appropriate alternative earns full credit. For example, where the scheme cites "spam filters" for supervised learning, credit medical image classification, credit scoring, handwriting recognition, sentiment analysis and any other valid instance. Where it cites Siri/Alexa as an AI application, credit any defensible application.
3. **MCQ (Q1).** One tick only. Two or more ticks = 0 for that item, even if one is correct. No half marks; no credit for annotation or working.
4. **Two-mark short answers (Q2).** Normally 1 mark for the core definition/statement and 1 for the required extension (example, contrast, consequence, or explanation of effect). Note Q2 instructs "answer in complete sentences", but **do not deduct for note form** — content is what is assessed. Spelling of technical terms is credited if the intended term is unambiguous (e.g. "algorythm", "superviced").
5. **Five-mark structured answers (Q3).** Apply point-plus-development: typically 3–4 marks for the required content and 1–2 for the mandated example(s). Where the stem says "include an example using a dataset" or "provide an example of each", the example marks cannot be recovered by additional theory. Where the stem says "identify three types … and describe where each might be applied", expect roughly 1 mark for naming and 1 for the application per type, with the fifth mark for accuracy/quality of the applications.
6. **Truth tables and logic.** Award per correct row. Accept T/F, True/False, 1/0, Y/N consistently used. A fully inverted table (e.g. AND logic applied to an OR table) earns 0, not partial credit for internal consistency.
7. **Pseudocode, flowcharts and rules.** Credit **logic over syntax**. IF–THEN rules, pseudocode and flowchart answers are marked on whether the reasoning is correct and unambiguous; do not penalise missing colons, non-standard keywords, absent END IF, or mixing Python-style and BASIC-style constructs. Flowchart shapes need not be conventional provided the sequence and decision points are legible. A rule written as prose ("if a car is detected and no pedestrian is crossing, the light turns green") is worth the same as one written in formal IF–THEN form.
8. **Diagrams.** The rubric permits diagrams "where helpful". A labelled diagram may earn full marks for a "describe" or "explain" item provided the labels carry the required meaning. Unlabelled diagrams earn nothing.
9. **Repetition.** A point already credited cannot be credited again in the same question, however it is rephrased. Across different questions, repetition is permissible.
10. **Blank / irrelevant.** Zero. Do not award "effort" marks. Material that is on-topic for AI but does not address the question (e.g. a history of AI in answer to an ethics question) earns nothing.
11. **Both extended options attempted (Q4).** Mark both and award the higher score, unless the candidate has clearly indicated which is to be marked.
12. **Overlength or continuation sheets.** Mark all of it. There is no penalty for exceeding the printed answer lines.
13. **Paper 2 authenticity.** Work must remain the learner's own; guidance is permitted. Where group work is undertaken, **individual contributions must be identified** — if they are not, Component C collaboration marks cannot be awarded above Low, and Component A marks must be evidenced by the teacher observation log. Supervision during model creation and testing is mandatory; unsupervised build work cannot be credited in Component A.
14. **Paper 2 submission completeness.** Missing the working model (or link) caps Component A at Low across training/testing and evaluation. Missing presentation material zeroes Component C system presentation and format.
15. **Best-fit judgement.** For all levelled items, select the band that best fits the response overall, then place within the band by the strength of the weaker criteria. Do not require every descriptor phrase to be met.

---

## 6. Common Student Errors and Their Cost

| Error | Where it appears | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| **Conflating training data and test data** — describing a model as "tested on the data it learned from". | Q2(c), Q4A, Paper 2 Component A/B. | Loses the AO1 mark for the distinction (spec 2.1.4, 6.1.4). In Paper 2, prevents "tested correctly" and caps model training and testing at Medium. |
| **Describing supervised learning without labels**, or offering clustering as an example of supervised learning. | Q1(b), Q3(c). | 0 for that item. The presence of *labelled* data is the defining feature. |
| **Naming a bias without stating its effect.** "AI can be biased" earns nothing; the mark requires the mechanism (unrepresentative training data) *and* the consequence (poor performance on under-represented groups, unfair outcomes). | Q2(d), Q5(c), Paper 2 Component B ethics. | Halves the available marks; caps Paper 2 ethics at Medium. |
| **Listing rather than comparing.** Two paragraphs, one on knowledge-based systems and one on ML, with no relational statement. | Q6. | Caps at Band 2 (max 5/10). |
| **Omitting the conclusion, or asserting one without justification.** | Q8. | Caps at Band 3 (max 8/10); an unjustified conclusion earns the conclusion structure mark only. |
| **Ignoring a printed bullet.** Answering only "advantages of AI in diagnostics" and never the risks; or covering data collection and training but not deployment/monitoring. | Q4, Q6, Q8. | Drops the response a full band. |
| **Generic ethics not tied to the scenario.** "AI raises privacy concerns" in a drone case study, with no reference to camera recording of streets, homes or bystanders. | Q5(c). | Identification mark only; no development mark. |
| **Confusing sensors with actuators** — attributing movement to sensors or perception to actuators. | Q4B, Q5(b). | Loses the AO1 accuracy credit and undermines the analysis marks that depend on it. |
| **"Advantages" that are not advantages of *AI*** — e.g. "drones are fast" rather than "AI enables real-time route optimisation and obstacle avoidance without a pilot". | Q5(a). | 1 of 2 marks at best. |
| **Truth-table errors from misreading the operator** (applying AND to an OR table). | Q7(a). | 0/4 — no partial credit for internal consistency. |
| **Restating the question as the answer.** "A decision tree works by making decisions in a tree." | Q3(a) and any "describe how" item. | 0. Requires splitting on feature values and reaching a classification at a leaf. |
| **Paper 2: evaluation with no refinement.** Candidate reports accuracy figures and stops. | Component A, evaluation and improvement. | Caps at Medium (6–8/10); High requires "clear refinements made". |
| **Paper 2: screenshots without commentary.** Images pasted with no caption or explanation. | Component B, visuals. | "Included, but not always clear or helpful" — Medium at best (3–4/5). |
| **Paper 2: reflection that is purely positive** ("it went well, I enjoyed it"). | Component C, personal reflection. | "Minimal or unclear reflection" — Low (1–2/5). High requires honesty about limitations and specific suggested improvements. |
| **Vague problem definition** ("build an AI"). | Component A. | Low (1–5). The problem must be "specific and realistic" for High. |

---

**Final instruction to markers:** annotate with the AO being credited on Paper 1 Section B and on all levelled items, record the band awarded before the mark, and retain Paper 2 teacher observation logs with the assessment forms for LRN external moderation.
